Guilty quarrels fill this verse: “throwing blame” (37:27). Blame thrown returns as blame shared. Shared blame burns no cooler. Cooler heads never enter this court. Courts of fire specialize in heat. Heat of quarrel preheats hell's chambers.

**From the Right Means From the Side of Power**

Arabic says the chiefs came *from the right*. *ʿAn al-yamīn*: from the right hand, the side of strength. Right hands seal oaths and wield swords. Chiefs approached with oaths and swords both. Promises allured; threats compelled. Translation renders the idiom as delusion from right guidance. Rendering interprets; interpretation here clarifies truly. Coming from the right meant coming as trusted counselors. Counselors of falsehood wore truth's wardrobe. Wardrobes of piety disguised wolves effectively. Wolves in wardrobes mislead sheep systematically. Sheep accuse shepherds when wolves arrive undisguised. Undisguised ruin ends all masquerades. Masquerades of dunyā dissolve at graves. Graves strip costumes from counselors. Counselors exposed face their counseled. Counseled crowds confront unmasked liars. Liars unmasked still lie about lying. Lying about lying doubles the guilt.

**You Deluded Us Pleads Seduction as Excuse**

*Aḍlaltumūnā* — you deluded us, you led us astray. Accusation doubles as exoneration plea. Pleas of seduction have ancient precedent. Adam blamed Eve; Eve blamed the serpent. Serpents get blamed; blamers still fall. Falling follows listening, whatever the voices. Voices of chiefs sounded sweet and sure. Sweetness of tone never licensed obedience. Obedience to creatures ends where disobedience to God begins. Beginnings of compromise end in pits. Pits receive seduced and seducers together. Togetherness in pits consoles no one. No seduction excuses surrendered reason. Reason surrendered answers for itself. Itself stands judged, not its seducers only. Seducers only share the dock, not the verdict's cause. Causes of ruin include invitations accepted. Accepted invitations bind acceptors eternally. Eternally bound, excuse-seekers find no exit. Exits from fire open for no one.

**What Is Right Was Never Hidden From Them**

*Ḥaqq* — the right, the true, the real — stood public. Messengers proclaimed it in every marketplace. Marketplaces heard; markets chose otherwise. Choices, not chances, damned the choosers. Choosers of falsehood now blame its salesmen. Salesmen of error advertised openly. Open advertisements deceive only willing buyers. Buyers of falsehood inspected the goods. Goods glittering with dunyā's glare blinded them. Blinding was voluntary throughout. Voluntary blindness pleads no mitigation. Mitigation requires ignorance, and knowledge abounded. Abundance of warning drowns excuses finally. Finally the weak confront the mighty in fire (40:47–48). Fires of confrontation illuminate old choices. Choices illuminated accuse choosers clearly. Clearly seeing, late seers weep vainly. Vain weeping waters no mercy. Mercies dried up with earthly mornings. Mornings of warning set forever. Forever the weak wish they had listened. Listening refused becomes wailing required.

**Pointing Upward Admits the Pointers Knew Up**

Accusation confesses knowledge obliquely. To blame misleaders, followers must know misleading. Knowing misleading means knowing leading. Leading known means truth was known. Knowledge admitted destroys ignorance pleas. Pleas of darkness fail from lamplighters. Lamplighters of excuse lit their own way to error. Errors chosen knowingly condemn doubly. Doubly damned: by deed and by discernment. Discernment unused testifies against its owners. Owners of insight abandoned it for comfort. Comfort of conformity cost eternity. Eternity lost for applause of crowds. Crowds applauded; crowds now accuse. Accusations of crowds indict crowds. Crowds indicting crowds convict all. All accusing all leaves none acquitted. Acquittals absent, sentences proceed. Proceedings of justice pause for no regrets. Regrets of the knowing burn hottest. Hottest regrets belong to clearest seers. Seers who saw and strayed suffer most. Most pitied, least excused: the knowing damned.

**The Charge Is True But Useless**

Chiefs did mislead; the charge states facts. Facts favor the followers partially. Partial truth makes potent poison. Poison of half-truth kills excuses. Excuses need whole truths to stand. Standing on halves topples accusers. Toppled accusers join their accused. Joined in fire, distinctions blur but remain. Remainders of rank persist in punishment. Punishments fit crimes with tailor's precision. Precision tailors extra torment for seducers. Seducers pay for seduction plus example. Examples corrupt multitudes beyond counting. Counting of victims multiplies guilt endlessly. Endlessly multiplied, guilt exceeds bearing. Bearing breaks; burning continues. Continues the fire, continues the blame. Blame continued changes nothing forever. Forever true, forever useless: the charge. Charges that convict others damn oneself. Oneself stands first among the accused. Accused majorities never acquit minorities. Minorities of chiefs fall with majorities of crowds.

**Blame Upward Precedes Excuse Downward**

Quarrels in fire follow fixed choreography. Followers accuse; chiefs will answer. Answers await their appointed verse. Verses ahead hold the chiefs' defense. Defenses of the damned persuade no one. No one arbitrates between burning parties. Parties burn while pleading simultaneously. Simultaneity of suffering mocks sequence of speeches. Speeches sequence for readers' instruction. Instruction emerges from futility displayed. Displayed futility warns living readers. Living readers may yet choose differently. Differently choosing requires present heeding. Heeding now prevents quarreling then. Then-quarrels rehearse in now-quarrels. Now-quarrels over truth foreshadow fire. Foreshadowed fates still permit escape. Escapes remain open while breath lasts. Last breaths close all exits. Exits closing counsel urgent return. Returns accepted need only sincerity. Sincerity now spares sophistry then. Sophistries of fire convince no judges. Judges of heaven weigh hearts truly.

**The Accused Get Their Turn to Answer**

Accusations complete, defense takes the floor. Floors of fire host formal rebuttals. Rebuttals of ruin persuade none. None arbitrates; both burn regardless. Regardless of rhetoric, verdicts stand fixed. Fixed verdicts mock fluent defenses. Defenses fluent in falsehood fail finally. Finally chiefs speak; followers listen unwillingly. Unwilling listeners hear unwelcome replies. Replies wound without acquitting. Acquittals absent, ashes accumulate. Accumulations of ash bury arguments. Arguments buried still burn unfelt. Unfelt burns consume unfelt denials. Denials unfelt fool no flames. Flames feel what speakers deny. Denied guilt burns brightest. Brightest burns mark blackest deeds. Deeds darkest draw deepest fires. Fires prepared welcome their fuel. The chiefs will answer the charge in their own voice, as the coming verse will show.
verses.29:
> The misleaders will reply, “No! You disbelieved on your own

**Denial Meets Denial: No Opens the Defense**

Chiefs answer charges with a slammed door. *Lā* — No! — the whole defense in one syllable. Syllables of denial match syllables of accusation. Accusation claimed delusion: “deluded us away from what is right” (37:28). Delusion alleged, delusion denied. Denied delusion still damned its deniers. Deniers of misleading stand convicted of it. Convictions precede confessions in this court. Courts of heaven convict before quarrels conclude. Conclusions of quarrels change no verdicts. Verdicts fixed before speeches began. Beginnings of blame end in shared fire. Fires shared warm no disputants. Disputants burn while denying together. Togetherness in denial mirrors togetherness in error. Errors together, denials together, fires together. Togetherness completes what solitude began. Began in markets, completed in flames. Flames complete every incomplete confession. Confessions incomplete still incriminate fully.

**On Your Own Returns Responsibility to Senders**

*Kuntum* — you were, yourselves — redirects every finger. Fingers pointed upward swing back downward. Downward they indicate willing breasts. Breasts that welcomed falsehood willingly. Willingness voids victimhood entirely. Victimhood requires coercion, and none occurred. Coercion absent, choice convicts. Choices of followers matched invitations of chiefs. Chiefs invited; followers RSVP'd with enthusiasm. Enthusiasm for error embarrasses excuses now. Excuses of compulsion collapse unbuilt. Unbuilt defenses shelter no defendants. Defendants of delusion stand self-condemned. Self-condemnation needs no prosecution. Prosecutions proceed regardless, for records demand it. Demands of records exceed needs of proof. Proofs abound where excuses evaporate. Evaporations of excuse leave guilt crystallized. Crystallized guilt refracts no mercy. Mercies refracted nowhere reach no one. No one reaches mercy through blame. Blame navigates nowhere but deeper fire. Fires deeper await blamers and blamed. Blamed and blaming burn side by side.

**The Defense Is Half True and Fully Insufficient**

Followers were willing; the defense states facts. Facts partial make defenses porous. Porous defenses leak under questioning. Questioning exposes omitted halves efficiently. Halves omitted include invitations issued. Issued invitations bear inviters' guilt. Guilt of inviters persists alongside guests'. Guests came willingly; hosts invited eagerly. Eagerness both ways doubles the damnation. Damnations doubled still burn singly. Singly each soul answers despite doubling. Doubling of guilt halves no sentence. Sentences full fall on partial pleaders. Pleaders of halves hear wholes in reply. Replies whole crush partial defenses. Defenses partial persuade no judges. Judges whole weigh halves exactly. Exactly weighed, halves condemn fully. Fully condemned, chiefs confess outcome. Outcomes confessed still damn confessors. Confessors of doom deny causes vainly. Vain denials of causes change nothing. Nothings changed, fires proceed apace. Apace the sentence nears completion.

**Chiefs Plead What Satan Will Plead**

Templates of evasion repeat across the damned. Satan himself will plead identically. Identically? Nearly: no authority, only invitation (14:22). Invitations accepted bind acceptors, pleads the devil. Devil's logic mirrors chiefs' logic exactly. Exactly parallel evasions damn parallel evaders. Evaders of responsibility meet inescapable reckoning. Reckonings inescapable terrify evaders most. Most evasive argue most vainly. Vainly pleaded, paradigmatic excuses fail. Failures of Satan foreshadow failures of chiefs. Chiefs echoing Satan share Satan's dock. Docks crowded with echoes amplify wailing. Wailing amplified fills the fire's acoustics. Acoustics of hell carry every excuse nowhere. Nowhere-bound excuses travel eternally. Eternally traveling, never arriving at acquittal. Acquittals never greet the guilty. Guilty pleaders plead to empty benches. Benches empty of mercy seat justice only. Justice only, mercy elsewhere, pity none. None pities pleaders who pitied none. None pitied in life pities in fire.

**No Coercion Means No Excuse for Either Side**

Freedom damns both parties equally. Chiefs chose to invite; followers chose to come. Coming and inviting meet in flames. Flames make no distinction of initiative. Initiatives of evil share single wages. Wages of invitation equal wages of acceptance. Acceptances willing match invitations eager. Eager invitations, willing acceptances, shared fires. Fires shared burn individually. Individual burns answer collective choices. Choices collective condense into fates personal. Personal fates reflect personal wills. Wills aligned in error diverge in blame. Blame diverged reunites in burning. Burning reunites what blame divided. Divided blamers, united burners. Burners united suffer severally. Severally suffered, jointly deserved. Deserved jointly, endured singly. Singly endured, eternally complete. Complete in suffering, incomplete in repentance. Repentance incomplete avails nothing. Nothings availed, fires prevail. Prevailing fires silence quarrels. Quarrels silenced leave only crackling.

**Doom Shared Gets Admitted Alongside Blame Refused**

Chiefs confess what they cannot contest. Contests over blame exclude contests over doom. Doom stands admitted by all parties: “we will certainly taste ˹the punishment˺” (37:31). Tasting certain needs no taster's consent. Consent irrelevant, consequence proceeds. Proceedings of doom pause for no pleas. Pleas about causes ignore effects decreed. Decreed effects execute themselves. Themselves executing, sentences need no bailiffs. Bailiffs of heaven watch otiose. Otiose observers witness automatic justice. Automatic does not mean unruled. Unruled never describes heaven's order. Orders of doom derive from decrees. Decrees of God govern every tasting. Tastings governed proceed on schedule. Schedules of torment never slip. Slips belong to earthly kitchens. Kitchens of hell serve punctually. Punctual servings sicken eternally. Eternally sickened, tasters taste on. Tasting continues; lessening never comes. No lessening, no ending. Endings absent, tastings abide.

**Quarrels of the Damned Entertain No One**

Spectatorship requires distance hell denies. Denied distance, all participate. Participation universal makes sport impossible. Impossible sports attract no audiences. Audiences absent, quarrels echo unheard. Unheard echoes still torment speakers. Speakers wound themselves with every word. Words of blame become brands of fire. Brands mark speakers permanently. Permanence of marks exceeds quarrels' span. Spans of quarrel end; marks remain. Remainders of ruin outlast rhetoric. Rhetoric exhausted, reality remains. Reality remaining is fire entire. Entire fires engulf entire quarrels. Quarrels engulfed fuel further flames. Flames further feed on foolishness. Foolishness fueling fires burns brightly. Brightly burning, blame illuminates guilt. Guilt illuminated needs no lamp. Lamps of quarrel light only loss. Losses lit appear total. Totals of loss exceed counting. Countings exceed, mercies recede. Receding mercies leave wrath alone.

**One Denial Prepares Another**

Defenses in fire follow choreography too. Denial opens; justification follows. Followings of denial deepen ditches. Ditches deepened trap diggers. Diggers of excuses fall inside. Inside ditches, darkness doubles. Doubling darkness blinds doubly. Doubly blinded, chiefs plead on. Pleadings on, flames approach. Approaches of fire quicken tongues. Tongues quickened stammer defenses. Stammered defenses convince no one. No one convinced, all condemned. Condemned chiefs continue pleading. Pleading continues; burning nears. Nearing fires hasten final pleas. Final pleas fail finally. Finally failing, chiefs face facts. Facts faced: doom certain, blame shared. Shared blame, certain doom, endless fire. Fires endless await pleas' end. Ends of pleading open torments. Torments opened never close. The chiefs will explain why the blame cannot stick, as the coming verse will show.
verses.30:
> We had no authority over you. In fact, you yourselves were a transgressing people

**No Authority Means No Compulsion, Not No Influence**

*Sulṭān* — authority, warrant, coercive proof — anchors the defense. Chiefs claim they wielded none over followers. Claims of impotence plead innocence by weakness. Weakness alleged, wickedness denied. Denied wickedness persists in records. Records show invitations, beautifications, threats. Threats unbacked by force still frightened. Frightened followers complied without chains. Chains absent, choices remained. Remaining choices condemn choosers. Choosers choosing error own outcomes. Outcomes owned cannot be disowned. Disowning attempted fails before facts. The denial this grounds was spoken just before: “You disbelieved on your own.” (37:29). Own-ness stressed, shared-ness suppressed. Suppressed sharing surfaces at sentencing. Sentencings surface all suppressions. Suppressions surface; surprises vanish. Vanish surprises; verdicts remain. Remainders of pleas dissolve. Dissolutions of defense delight justice. Justice delighted proceeds unimpeded. Unimpeded proceedings conclude swiftly. Swift conclusions stun slow pleaders.

**Satan's Speech Supplies the Template**

Chiefs plagiarize hell's oldest defendant. Satan's acquittal speech survives in the Book. No authority had I, he pleads, save calling (14:22). Calling voice, coming feet: responsibility stays with comers. Comers blame callers vainly. Vain blaming echoes through fire. Fires of hell amplify ancient excuses. Excuses ancient fail freshly. Fresh failures repeat old patterns. Patterns of evasion never evolve. Evolutions absent, repetitions reign. Reigns of repetition bore no one. Boredom absent, terror present. Present terrors teach timeless lessons. Lessons timeless: blame yourselves, not me. Me-blaming fails; self-blaming saves none either. Either way, fire receives both. Both caller and comer burn. Burning together, blaming apart. Apart in blame, together in flame. Flames together seal fates apart. Fates apart in degree, together in kind. Kinds of torment vary; fact remains. Remainders of excuse perish.

**Influence Without Force Still Earns the Fire**

Compulsion's absence never equaled innocence. Innocence requires clean hands, not weak ones. Hands of chiefs beckoned generations astray. Astray beckoned, multitudes followed. Followed beckonings bind beckoners. Beckoners bear double burdens. Burdens doubled: own error plus others'. Others' burdens pile on inviters (29:13). Inviters of error inherit followers' weight. Weights inherited crush preachers of falsehood. Falsehoods preached profit nothing. Nothings profited, torments multiplied. Multiplied torments match multiplied victims. Victims multiplied by eloquence. Eloquence of error damns the eloquent. Eloquent damned outsuffer silent sinners. Sinners silent burn for selves alone. Alone-burning beats burden-bearing. Bearing others' burdens breaks chiefs. Chiefs broken beggar description. Descriptions beggared, fires suffice. Sufficient fires need no adjectives. Adjectives absent, agonies present. Present agonies teach absent heeders. Heeders absent from warnings attend fires. Fires attended instruct eternally. Eternally instructed, never released.

**Transgressing People Turns the Charge Around**

*Ṭāghīn* — transgressing, rebellious, overstepping — flies back upward. Upward charges return downward doubled. Doubled charges damn both directions. Directions of blame crossfire. Crossfires in quarrels wound all. Wounds all around attest universal guilt. Guilt universal needs no allocation. Allocations attempted fail. Failures of allocation prove abundance of guilt. Abundance of guilt exceeds excuses. Excuses exceeded collapse. Collapses of excuse bury pleaders. Pleaders buried plead no more. Mores of mercy never reach them. Them reached only wrath entire. Entire wrath meets entire rebellion. Rebellions entire earn fires entire. Entire fires greet entire transgressors. Transgressors entire, excuses none. Nones of excuse, alls of guilt. Guilts of all condemn each. Each condemned, all burning. Burning all, blaming each. Each blamed, all burning. Burnings mutual, mercies absent. Absences of mercy complete sentences. Sentences complete, quarrels continue. Continuing quarrels change nothing.

**Both Verdicts Can Be True at Once**

Chiefs misled; followers transgressed. Transgressed followers followed misleading chiefs. Chiefs misleading, followers straying: both burning. Burning both, justice distinguishes. Distinguishes degrees, unites fates. Fates united in fire, degrees distinct in depth. Depths of fire fit heights of guilt. Guilt's heights measured precisely. Precisely measured, perfectly punished. Perfect punishments brook no appeals. Appeals absent, justice stands. Stands justice, falls excuse. Excuses fallen fertilize nothing. Nothings fertilized grow only flames. Flames grown from excuses burn hottest. Hottest flames greet greatest misleaders. Misleaders greatest suffer deepest. Deepest sufferings match highest platforms. Platforms highest fall farthest. Farthest falls shatter most. Most shattered, least pitied. Pitied least, punished most. Most punished, first blamed. Blamed first by followers. Followers blaming, chiefs denying. Denying chiefs, burning both. Both burning ends the dispute.

**In Fact Corrects the Followers' Self-Portrait**

*Bal* returns to revise sympathies. Sympathies for followers seemed natural. Natural sympathies misread the scene. Scenes of shared guilt permit none. Nones of pity greet volunteers. Volunteers for error chose openly. Openly choosing, secretly regretting. Regretting secretly saves nothing. Nothings saved, all sentenced. Sentenced volunteers join volunteering chiefs. Chiefs volunteering invitations meet volunteers accepting. Accepting volunteers complete the circuit. Circuits complete conduct fire. Fires conducted burn circuits. Circuits burning, sympathies wither. Withered sympathies feed no appeals. Appeals unfed starve quickly. Quickly starved, hopes die. Dies hope, lives horror. Horrors living outlast hopes dead. Dead hopes bury living rebels. Rebels buried burn on. Burnings on, endings none. Nones of ending, alls of ache. Aches of all fill fire. Fires filled, quarrels proceed. Proceedings proceed; pity pauses.

**Excuses Exhaust Themselves Before the Sentence**

Arguments consume their own fuel. Fuels of falsehood burn quickly. Quickly burnt, excuses ash. Ashes of argument choke pleaders. Pleaders choking fall silent. Silences of exhaustion precede sentences. Sentences proceeding need no consent. Consents unneeded, consequences roll. Rolling consequences crush lingering pleas. Pleas lingering die unheard. Unheard pleas haunt no judges. Judges unthreatened proceed calmly. Calm proceedings terrify most. Most terrifying: order amid horror. Horrors ordered proceed punctually. Punctually proceeding, sentences land. Landings of verdicts shake plains. Plains shaken settle into silence. Silences settled seal fates. Fates sealed admit no appeals. Appeals admitted nowhere ever. Evers of denial end. Endings of excuse begin torments. Torments begun never conclude. Conclusions absent, pains persist. Persists pain, perishes hope. Hopes perished, horror reigns. Reigns horror, endless, entire.

**Quarrel Ends Where Sentence Begins**

Quarrels exhausted, both parties face forward. Forward faces the bench. Benches of heaven seat one Judge. Judges singular judge plurally guilty. Guilty plural hear singular verdicts. Verdicts singular cover multitudes. Multitudes covered cower together. Together cowering, separately sentenced. Sentenced singly, suffering jointly. Jointly suffering, singly responsible. Responsible singly, ruined together. Togethers of ruin mirror togethers of error. Errors together, ruins together. Togethers twin: sinning, suffering. Sufferings twin with sins exactly. Exactly twinned, eternally bound. Bound eternally, quarrels cease. Ceasings of quarrel open silences. Silences of sentence awe all. All awed, none acquitted. Acquitted none, sentenced all. All sentenced: the sentence nears. Nearing sentences silence quarrels. Quarrels silenced, fates sealed. Quarrel spent, both parties face what neither can dispute, as the coming verse will show.
verses.31:
> The decree of our Lord has come to pass against us ˹all˺: we will certainly taste ˹the punishment˺

**Confession Replaces Contention at Last**

Quarrels exhaust themselves; confession begins. *Ḥaqqa ʿalaynā qawlu rabbinā*: our Lord's decree proved true against us. Proved-true verdicts end all pleading. Pleadings of followers and chiefs alike fall silent. Silences of admission replace noises of blame. Blame's noises fade; truth's silence reigns. Reigns of truth admit no rivals. Rivals in quarrel unite in confession. Confessions united seal fates jointly. Jointly sealed, doom stands certain. Certainties confessed need no enforcement. Enforcements unnecessary where admission suffices. Sufficiencies of confession close the docket. Dockets closed proceed to tasting. Tastings follow confessions on schedule. Schedules kept punish punctually. Punctual punishments teach timeless lessons. Lessons timeless outlive learners. Learners perished, lessons persist. Persists the decree, perishes the denier. Deniers perished confess eternally. Eternal confessions convince none. Nones convinced: mercy closed.

**Our Lord Confesses What Their Lips Long Denied**

*Rabbinā* — our Lord — slips from deniers' lips. Lips that denied lordship now own it. Owned lordship confessed too late. Lateness voids the confession's value. Values of faith expire at sight. Sights of doom compel admissions. Admissions compelled convince no courts. Courts of heaven weigh timing. Timings late forfeit mercies. Mercies forfeited return never. Nevers of mercy last forever. Forevers of loss begin here. Beginnings of loss end hopes. Hopes ended leave only tasting. Tastings certain await confessors. Confessors certain of doom. Dooms certain admit no delay. Delays expired with earthly dawns. Dawns earthly set forever. Forevers begun never end. Endings absent, pains persist. Persists pain, perishes pride. Prides perished confess truly. Truly confessed, still damned.

**Against Us All Levels Leaders and Led**

*ʿAlaynā* — against us — gathers every party. Parties to quarrel share single prepositions. Prepositions of doom admit no exceptions. Exceptions expired with excuses. Excuses expired, equality reigns. Reigns of equality level hierarchies. Hierarchies leveled: chiefs beside crowds. Crowds beside chiefs: all againsted. All againsted by a single decree. Decrees single cover multitudes. Multitudes covered confess together. Together confessing, the old defense dies: “We had no authority over you” (37:30). Authority denied, doom admitted. Admitted doom ends denials. Denials ended, fires near. Nearing fires silence boasts. Boasts silenced, truths spoken. Truth spoken damns speakers. Speakers damned fall silent. Silences final precede flames. Flames final finish quarrels. Quarrels finished, tastings start. Starts of tasting never stop. Stoppings none, tastings ever. Evers of tasting exhaust never.

**Come to Pass Means Prophecy Fulfilled Exactly**

*Ḥaqqa* — it proved true, it came to pass. Passings of decrees never miss. Missings none: heaven aims perfectly. Perfect aims strike appointed souls. Souls appointed receive prophecies. Prophecies received in scorn return in fire. Fires of fulfillment warm warners. Warners warmed watch vindicated. Vindications of messengers complete arcs. Arcs complete: warned, scorned, fulfilled. Fulfilled warnings damn scorners. Scorners damned confess accuracy. Accuracy confessed vindicates warners. Warners vindicated, deniers tasted. Tasted deniers affirm prophecies. Prophecies affirmed too late. Latenesses fatal recur eternally. Eternal recurrences teach the living. Livings taught may yet heed. Heedings now prevent tastings then. Thens of tasting follow nows of scorning. Scornings now purchase pains then. Purchases of pain prove foolish. Foolish purchases void no sales. Sales final, refunds none. Nones of refund, alls of regret.

**We Will Certainly Taste Adds Bodies to Verdicts**

*Dhāʾiqūn* — tasters, we shall taste. Tastes of fire touch tongues. Tongues that sneered will savor flames. Flames savored sicken tasters. Tasters sickened taste on. Tastings on admit no pause. Pauses none; pains constant. Constants of pain define eternity. Eternities defined exclude relief. Reliefs excluded, despairs reign. Reigns of despair darken tastings. Darkened tastings disgust eternally. Eternally disgusted, tasters continue. Continuations endless weary none. Weariless pains persist precisely. Precise persistences punish perfectly. Perfect punishments fit crimes exactly. Exact fits tailor torments. Tailored torments clothe criminals. Clothed criminals wear fires. Fires worn never removed. Removals none; wearings eternal. Eternal wearings chafe ceaselessly. Ceaseless chafings gall tasters. Tasters galled taste gall. Galls of fire sicken souls. Souls sickened faint never. Nevers of fainting last forever. Forevers of tasting begin now.

**The Punishment Needs No Adjective Here**

*Al-ʿadhāb* — the punishment, known, definite. Definiteness assumes familiarity. Familiar punishments frighten most. Most-frightening: threats long heard. Heard threats materialize. Materialized threats terrify fulfilled. Fulfilled terrors exceed imaginings. Imaginings exceeded, horrors reign. Reigns of horror need no adjectives. Adjectives absent; articles suffice. Sufficiencies of *the* condemn fully. Fully condemned by two letters. Letters of definiteness seal doom. Dooms sealed open never. Nevers of opening last forever. Forevers sealed admit no visitors. Visitors none; residents eternal. Residents eternal know the punishment. Known punishments punish knowingly. Knowing punishments fit knowers. Knowers fitted suffer precisely. Precise sufferings satisfy justice. Justice satisfied rests never. Rests never taken in fire. Fires restless burn residents. Residents burning know fully. Fully known, fully tasted. Tastings of the known torment. Torments known exceed unknown.

**Confession Completes the Leaders' Arc**

Leaders denied, excused, now confess. Confessions final end performances. Performances ended: denials, excuses, evasions. Evasions ended, truths emerge. Emerging truths damn their speakers. Speakers damned by honesty. Honesties late save none. Nones saved by timing's miss. Misses of timing prove fatal. Fatal misses recur as warnings. Warnings to leaders living now. Living leaders may confess early. Early confessions open mercies. Mercies opened await entrants. Entrants entering find welcome. Welcomes warm greet penitents. Penitents greeted gain pardon. Pardons gained erase dooms. Dooms erased, fates rewritten. Rewritten fates favor the early. Early favored, late condemned. Condemned late confess vainly. Vain confessions echo: “You disbelieved on your own.” (37:29). Own-ness once flung returns. Returns of denials boomerang. Boomeranged blame strikes blamers. Blamers struck confess jointly. Joint confessions close arcs.

**Confession Widens From Fate to Fault**

Dooms confessed; deeds await naming. Namings of deeds particularize guilt. Guilt particularized pierces deeper. Deeper piercings pain precisely. Precise pains teach publicly. Public teachings warn multitudes. Multitudes warned may repent. Possible repentance persists for the living. Livings repenting escape tastings. Tastings escaped by few. Fews escaping enter gardens. Gardens entered reward early. Early rewarded, late tasting. Tastings late last forever. Forevers tasting sicken souls. Souls sickened confess on. Confessings on convince none. Nones convinced, dooms certain. Certain dooms follow vague denials. Denials vague collapse specific. Specifics of guilt emerge next. Emergings of specifics near. Nearings of naming approach. Approachings of confession quicken. Quickenings of doom hasten. Hastenings end in naming. Namings of deeds damn doubly. Doubly damned: doomed and detailed. Confession widens from fate to fault, as the coming verse will show.
verses.32:
> We caused you to deviate, for we ourselves were deviant.”

**Caused to Deviate Confesses the Crime**

*Aghwaynākum* — We caused you to deviate. Misled-yous confess misleading. Misleadings confessed damn confessors. Confessors damned speak truly. Truly spoken, truly damning. Damning truths need no polish. Polishes absent, guilt gleams. Gleaming guilt blinds pleaders. Blinded pleaders stumble sentenced. Sentenced stumblers fall flaming. Flaming falls finish quarrels. Finished quarrels yield tastings, as the leaders confess: “we will certainly taste ˹the punishment˺” (37:31). Tastings yielded last forever. Forevers yielded never return. Returns never granted in fire. Fires grant no returns. Returns refused, regrets retained. Retained regrets torment tasters. Tasters tormented taste on. Tastings on, pleadings off. Pleadings off, pains on. Pains on, hopes off. Hopes off, horrors on. Horrors on, mercies off. Mercies off forevermore. Forevermores of loss begin. Begun losses never end. Ended never, pains persist. Persists pain, perishes plea. Pleas perished leave silence. Silences of guilt deafen. Deafened heavens hear none.

**The Charge Returns as Confession**

Followers charged delusion earlier. Earlier charges echo now. Echoings of charges convict. Convicted chargers confess charges. Charges confessed: delusion admitted. Admitted delusions damn admitters. Admitters damned speak the charge itself: “deluded us away from what is right” (37:28). Rights abandoned, wrongs embraced. Embraced wrongs strangle embracers. Embracers strangled gasp guilty. Guilty gasps convince none. Nones convinced hear more. Mores of confession continue. Continued confessions compound guilt. Guilts compounded crush confessors. Crushed confessors confess more. Mores of guilt emerge. Emergings of guilt glare. Glarings of guilt blind. Blinded by guilt, chiefs babble. Babblings of chiefs damn crowds. Crowds damned curse chiefs. Chiefs cursed curse back. Back-cursings fill fires. Fires filled with cursings. Cursings filling fires fuel flames. Flames fueled burn cursers. Cursers burning curse on. Cursings on, blessings none. Blessings none ever enter. Enters never mercy here. Heres of horror last.

**For We Ourselves Were Deviant Explains Without Excusing**

*Ghāwīn* — deviant, erring, lost. Lost leaders led multitudes astray. Astray-multitudes follow astray-chiefs. Astray chiefs plead their straying. Strayings pleaded explain nothing. Nothings explained excuse none. Nones excused by causes. Causes cited condemn citers. Citers condemned cite more. Mores cited damn deeper. Deeper damnings need no causes. Causes needless, guilt remains. Remainings of guilt persist. Persists guilt, perishes excuse. Excuses perished plead never. Nevers of excuse last. Lastings of loss begin. Begun losses compound. Compounded losses crush. Crushed by loss, chiefs confess. Confessings of chiefs continue. Continuings of confession weary none. Weariless confessions damn doubly. Doubly damned: stray and straying. Strayings of self precede. Precedings of self-straying cause. Causings of ruin remain. Remainings of ruin testify. Testifyings of ruin condemn. Condemnings certain proceed. Proceedings certain conclude. Concludings certain damn. Damnings certain last. Lastings eternal begin.

**Stray Guides Lead Convoys Over Cliffs**

Guides astray guide astray. Astray-guidings doom convoys. Convoys doomed follow blindly. Blind followers fall off cliffs. Cliffs of error await. Awaitings of cliffs certain. Certain ruins approach. Approachings of ruin hasten. Hastenings of doom quicken. Quickenings of fire near. Nearings of flame terrify. Terrifying flames precede tastings. Tastings preceded terrify doubly. Doubly terrified, convoys confess. Confessings of convoys continue. Continuings of confession compound. Compoundings of guilt crush. Crushings of guilt powder. Powdered guilt chokes. Chokings of powder blind. Blindings of powder darken. Darkenings of doom deepen. Deepenings of darkness last. Lastings of darkness never lift. Liftings never granted. Granted never mercy. Mercies never granted return. Returns never granted stand. Standings of refusal last. Lastings of refusal harden. Hardenings of refusal petrify. Petrified refusals mock pleadings. Pleadings mocked fall silent. Silences mocked damn deeper. Burdens of the misled pile on misleaders (16:25).

**Astray First, Misleading Second: Order Matters**

Self-straying precedes other-misleading. Misleadings follow strayings. Strayings first, misleadings after. Afters of straying mislead. Misleadings of the astray damn doubly. Doubly damned: self, others. Others damned damn damners. Damners damned doubly suffer. Doubly sufferings never lighten. Lightenings never granted. Granted nevers last. Lastings of weight crush. Crushings of weight powder. Powderings of chiefs choke. Chokings of dust blind. Blindings of dust deepen. Deepenings of gloom last. Lastings of gloom persist. Persistings of gloom punish. Punishings of gloom perfect. Perfectings of pain last. Lastings of pain never lift. Liftings never come. Comings never promised. Promised nevers hold. Holdings of never last. Lastings of never harden. Hardenings of never petrify. Petrifyings of never mock. Mockings of never damn. Damned in order, suffering sequenced. Sequenced sufferings fit sequenced sins. Sins sequenced: stray, then straying. Strayings after strayings compound. Compounded orders crush chiefs.

**Confession Without Repentance Seals the File**

*Iqrār* admits; *tawbah* returns. Returns absent, admissions damn. Damnings of admission last. Lastings of iqrār harden. Hardenings of file seal. Sealings of file final. Finals of sealing stand. Standings of seals last. Lastings of seals never break. Breakings never granted seals. Seal-granted nevers hold. Holdings of seals harden. Hardenings of holdings petrify. Petrifyings of files mock. Mockings of files damn. Damned by files, chiefs burn. Burnings of files light. Lightings of files glare. Glarings of files blind. Blindings of files darken. Darkenings of files deepen. Deepenings of files last. Lastings of files never lift. Liftings never granted files. Files never lifted stand. Standings of files accuse. Accusings of files convict. Convictings of files conclude. Concludings of files damn. Damned by conclusions, all burn. Burnings of conclusions light. Lightings of doom glare. Glarings of doom blind. Blind by glare, none escape. Escapes none granted ever. Evers of denial end.

**Leaders' Doom Doubles: Stray and Straying**

Self-guilt plus other-guilt. Guilt-doubled crushes doubly. Doubly crushed, chiefs confess. Confessings double with guilt. Guilt doubled, doom doubled. Doubled dooms last doubly. Doubly-lasts never lighten. Lightenings never granted doubly. Doubly-granted nevers hold. Holdings double harden double. Doubles doubling damn doubly. Doubly damned doubly confess. Confessings doubly damn doubly. Doublys of doom last. Lastings double never lift. Liftings never granted doubles. Doubles never lifted stand. Standings of doubles accuse. Accusings of doubles convict. Convictings of doubles conclude. Concludings of doubles damn. Damned by doubling, chiefs burn. Burnings of doubles light. Lightings of doubles glare. Glarings of doubles blind. Blindings of doubles darken. Darkenings of doubles deepen. Deepenings of doubles last. Lastings of doubles never lift. Liftings never come for doubles. Doubles unlifted stand eternal. Eternals of doubling last. Lastings eternal never end. Endings never granted doubles. Doubles endless, mercies none.

**Particular Confessions Yield to Universal Sentence**

Confessions particular conclude. Concluded particulars yield to generals. Generals of sentence approach. Approachings of sentence hasten. Hastenings of sentence quicken. Quickenings of sentence near. Nearings of sentence terrify. Terrifying sentences precede tastings. Preceded tastings terrify doubly. Doubly terrified, all confess. Confessings of all continue. Continuings of confession tire none. Tirings none granted. Granted refusals last. Lastings of refusal petrify. Petrifyings of refusal mock. Mockings of refusal damn. Damned by refusal, all burn. Refusals burning light the fire. Fires lit by refusal. Refusal-lit fires glare. Glarings of refusal blind. Blinded by refusal, none escape. Escapes none; sentences near. Nearing sentences silence pleas. Silenced pleas damn deeper. Deeper damnings need no words. Words needless, fires speak. Speakings of fire convince. Convinced none escape. Confession complete, heaven pronounces the sentence, as the coming verse will show.
verses.33:
> Surely on that Day they will ˹all˺ share in the punishment

**Quarrel Ends in Commons, Not Verdicts**

No gavel falls between followers and chiefs. Heaven issues no winner's certificate here. Instead all parties receive identical portions. Portions identical: fire, shared, entire. *Mushtarikūn* — sharers, partners, co-owners of torment. Partnership in error matures into partnership in pain. Maturation completes what seduction started. Started together, ended together. Together-ness seals what apart-ness argued. Argued apart, sealed together. Sealings of sharing last forever. Forevers of sharing never divide. Divisions none; commons entire — “we ourselves were deviant” (37:32). Astray together, tasting together. Togethers of tasting last. Lastings of commons never lift. Liftings never granted commons. Commons eternal, sharers damned. Damned sharers share doubly. Doubly sharing, singly suffering. Sufferings single, sentences shared. Shared sentences stand eternal. Eternals of sharing frighten. Frightened sharers share on. Sharings on never cease.

**Turning Together Ends in Burning Together**

The quarrel's circle closes in this verse. Turning began the dispute; sharing ends it. *Aqbalū* opened; *mushtarikūn* closes. Openings of quarrel promised speeches. Speeches delivered damned speakers. Speakers damned share dockets. Dockets shared yield sentences shared. Sentences shared: fire entire. Entire fires greet entire quarrels. Quarrels entire end entire. Endings entire close circles. Circles closed recall openings: “turn on each other” (37:27). Openings recalled damn doubly. Doubly damned: turning, tasting. Turnings to blame, tastings of fire. Fires of tasting greet turners. Turners greeted burn together. Togethers of burning last. Lastings of burning never lift. Liftings never granted burners. Burners unlifted stand eternal. Eternals of burning frighten. Frightened burners burn on. Burnings on never cease. Ceasings never granted fires. Fires unceasing punish perfectly. Perfect punishments fit turners.

**All Closes the Last Exit of Exception**

*Jamīʿ* — all, every, without exception. Exceptions sought, exceptions denied. Denied exceptions damn hopers. Hopers of exemption hope vainly. Vain hopes feed hotter fires. Hotter fires greet all alike. Alike in fire: chiefs, crowds. Crowds and chiefs, all tasting. Tastings of all last all. Alls of tasting never end. Endings none for any. Anys of exemption vanish. Vanished exemptions mock hopers. Mocked hopers hope never. Nevers of hope last. Lastings of hopelessness harden. Hardenings of hopelessness petrify. Petrified hopelessness mocks mercy. Mercies mocked withdraw. Withdrawn mercies return never. Nevers of return last. Lastings of never harden. Hardenings of never petrify. Petrifyings of never mock. Mockings of never damn. Damned by never, all burn. Burnings of all light. Lightings of all glare. Glarings of all blind.

**Sharing Punishment Multiplies Rather Than Divides**

Shared burdens lighten on earth. Earthly sharings halve weights. Halved weights comfort carriers. Carriers comforted thank sharers. Thanked sharers share more. Mores of sharing ease earth. Earthly eases end at graves. Graves open onto reversals. Reversals of sharing shock. Shocked sharers learn arithmetic. Arithmetics of fire: shared means multiplied. Multiplied shares crush sharers. Crushings of shares powder. Powdered sharers choke. Chokings of sharers blind. Blindings of sharers darken. Darkenings of sharers deepen. Deepenings of sharers last. Lastings of sharers never lift. Liftings never granted sharers. Sharers unlifted stand eternal. Eternals of sharers last. Lastings eternal never end. Endings never granted sharers. Sharers endless, mercies none. Nones of mercy last. Lastings of nones harden. Hardenings of nones petrify. Petrified nones mock hopes. Hopes mocked die doubly. Doubly dead hopes damn.

**On That Day Dates the Sharing**

*Yawmaʾidhin* — on that Day, then. Thens of sharing follow nows of straying. Strayings now purchase sharings then. Purchases of pain prove final. Finals of purchase stand. Standings of finals last. Lastings of finals never lift. Liftings never granted finals. Finals unlifted stand eternal. Eternals of finals last. Lastings eternal never end. Endings never granted finals. Finals endless, sharings entire. Entire sharings greet all. Alls greeted burn together. Togethers of burning last. Lastings of burning never lift. Liftings never granted burners. Burners unlifted stand eternal. Eternals of burning frighten. Frightened burners burn on. Burnings on never cease. Ceasings never granted fires. Fires unceasing punish perfectly. Perfect punishments fit sharers. Sharers fitted suffer precisely. Precise sufferings satisfy justice. Justice satisfied rests never. Rests never taken. Takens never granted. Granted nevers hold eternal.

**Surely Seals What Quarrels Questioned**

*Inna* — surely, truly, certainly. Certainties of heaven close debates. Debates closed, quarrels ended. Ended quarrels yield sentences. Sentences yielded stand sure. Sure standings last forever. Forevers sure never shake. Shakings never granted certainties. Certainties unshaken stand eternal. Eternals certain frighten doubters. Doubters frightened doubt never. Nevers of doubt last. Lastings of certainty harden. Hardenings of certainty petrify. Petrified certainties mock doubters. Doubters mocked doubt vainly. Vain doubtings damn doubly. Doubly damned doubters confess. Confessings of doubters continue. Continuings of confession tire none. Tirings none granted. Granted tirings never come. Comings never promised tirings. Promised nevers hold. Holdings of never last. Lastings of never harden. Hardenings of never petrify. Petrifyings of never mock. Mockings of never damn. Damned by mocking, doubters burn. Burnings of doubters light. Lightings of doubters glare. Glarings of doubters blind. Blinded doubters doubt never.

**The Punishment Gathers All Its Earners**

*Al-ʿadhāb* collects its earners. Earners earned; collectors collect. Collections complete, distributions start. Distributions of fire fit all. Alls fitted suffer alike. Alike sufferings satisfy ledgers. Ledgers balanced close forever. Forevers of balance last. Lastings of balance never shake. Shakings never granted balances. Balances unshaken stand eternal. Eternals balanced frighten earners. Earners frightened earn never. Nevers of earning last. Lastings of never harden. Hardenings of never petrify. Petrifyings of never mock. Mockings of never damn. Damned by never, earners burn. Burnings of earners light. Lightings of earners glare. Glarings of earners blind. Blinded earners earn never. Earning never, burning ever. Burnings ever last eternal. Eternals ever never end. Endings never granted burnings. Burnings endless, earners wailing. Wailings endless fill fires. Fires filled with wailings. Wailings filling fires fuel flames. Flames fueled burn wailers. Wailers burning wail on.

**One Sentence Becomes a Standing Rule**

Particulars judged yield universals. Universals of judgment stand. Standings of universals last. Lastings of universals never shake. Shakings never granted rules. Rules unshaken stand eternal. Eternals of rules frighten. Frightened hearers heed perhaps. Perhaps-heedings save some. Some saved escape sharing. Sharings escaped by few. Fews escaping enter gardens. Gardens entered reward early. Early rewarded, late sharing. Sharings late last forever. Forevers sharing sicken souls. Souls sickened share on. Sharings on convince none. Nones convinced, sentences certain. Certain sentences follow sure words. Sure words seal quarrels. Sealed quarrels yield rules. Rules yielded warn living. Livings warned may repent. Repentings now prevent sharings. Sharings prevented save souls. Souls saved praise mercy. Mercies praised open wider. Wider mercies welcome more. Mores of mercy save. Saved by mercy, few rejoice. Rejoicings of saved last. Heaven draws the standing moral, as the coming verse will show.
verses.34:

verses.41:
> They will have a known provision

**A Known Provision Answers the Hunger of Uncertainty**

Certainty is the first course of the meal. Rizqun maʿlūm — a provision known — promises not only food but freedom from the oldest anxiety about food: whether it will come, how much will come, and how long it will last. Al-Qurṭubī's reading, often quoted on this verse, turns on exactly that contrast: in the present world no heart is ever fully free of the fear that today's blessing may vanish by tomorrow, while the provision of the Garden is certain and everlasting at once. The adjective therefore does double work. It describes the food, which arrives in kinds the eaters recognize, and it describes the eaters' knowledge, which is free of calculation and dread. The recipients were named in the previous verse — “the chosen servants of Allah” (37:40) — and naming precedes feeding for a reason: belonging is established before bounty begins. Earthly tables seat strangers and rivals together; this table seats only those already claimed. The verse ends with a colon rather than a stop, so the provision is announced here and itemized next: hunger of the body is answered by fruits, and hunger of the mind — the need to know — is answered first.

**Known Can Mean Fixed in Time**

A second reading hears schedule in the adjective. On this view maʿlūm means appointed at known times: the provision arrives morning and evening with a punctuality the present world never quite keeps. The cross-reference is Maryam, where the Garden's people receive their provision “morning and evening” (19:62) — a phrase the commentators quote here almost by reflex. The strength of the reading is its concreteness: eternity is not formless duration but a rhythm of renewed arrivals, each one expected and each one fresh. Against it stands the question of whether Paradise keeps hours at all, since its light never fails and its people never tire. The two readings need not compete. A provision can be both certain in substance and appointed in season; indeed that combination is precisely what earthly provision lacks, arriving either irregularly or anxiously or both. What turns on the debate is the texture of bliss: whether the Garden's joy is a steady state or a repeated event. The verse allows both, and the wisest commentaries refuse to choose.

**Known Can Mean Described in Advance**

A third reading points the adjective at revelation's audience rather than the eater. The provision is known because the Qur'an has already described it in detail across other sūrahs: the fruits and fowl, the cups and couches, the shade and streams. Thanawi preferred this sense, and its ground is textual rather than speculative — the Book does in fact itemize the Garden's menu at length, so that believers arrive already acquainted with what awaits them. The attraction of the view is pastoral: revelation lets its people preview their wages, and previewed wages strengthen present patience. Its limit is that it makes maʿlūm describe our knowledge, while the verse's grammar seats the provision among theirs. Yet the two directions meet without strain. A provision described here and recognized there is doubly known, and recognition is itself a pleasure: the authentication of every promise at the moment of tasting. The readings differ on whose knowledge counts; the verse is generous enough to count both.

**Provision Here Means Pleasure, Not Survival**

The word rizq itself changes meaning at the Garden's gate. In the present world provision is what keeps the living alive: calories against hunger, wages against want. In the Garden nothing needs keeping, because no one hungers, thirsts, tires, or ages. Al-Rāzī drew the consequence sharply in connection with the fruits below: the cuisine of Paradise exists for taste rather than need, for the fulfillment of wish rather than the repair of weakness. Provision thus survives its own purpose and becomes pure gift — not fuel but favor. The symmetry with the previous passage is exact and deliberate. The deniers were told they would taste torment as wages — “rewarded for what you used to do” (37:39) — and the servants are told they will receive provision as wages. Both parties taste what they earned; the earnings differ absolutely. Justice gives each mouth what its life ordered. The verse therefore belongs as much to the doctrine of recompense as to the description of bliss: provision is not scenery, it is salary.

**The Garden Itself or the Goods Within It**

The earliest readers disagreed about the noun before they ever reached the adjective. Some — the traditions associated with Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Kathīr — took “provision” to mean the Garden itself, the whole estate granted as one bounty. Others — Ṭabarī and Zamakhsharī among them — took it to mean the goods within the Garden, the fruits and drinks itemized in the verses ahead. The first view leans on the word's breadth: rizq in the Qur'an can cover anything granted, including shelter, status, and spouses, so the Garden entire is one provision. The second leans on the context: what follows is a menu, not a map, and menus list goods. Each side's ground is genuine, and the verse may intend the overlap. A place is known by what it provides, and bounty unnamed is bounty unrecognized; calling the Garden “provision” names it by its generosity. The colon at the verse's end favors the second view for what follows, without canceling the first for what is meant.

**Honor Frames the Whole Menu**

Possession without labor is the quietest luxury in the verse. “They will have” — the verb gives without demanding: no sowing, no earning, no carrying, no cooking. Earthly provision always arrives with a bill attached, whether paid in sweat, anxiety, or gratitude owed to intermediaries. The Garden's provision arrives the way gifts arrive, and the eaters receive it the way guests receive, which is why the tradition counts honor itself among the courses. Zamakhsharī's remark that being honored is the greatest recompense belongs exactly here: the food matters, but the status of those fed matters more. Dignity is the dish no earthly table can serve, because every earthly host can withdraw it. Here the Host cannot withdraw it, since the provision is known — fixed, certain, and everlasting. To be fed without being made small is the difference between wages and charity, and Paradise pays wages. What the provision contains comes next, as the coming verse will show.
verses.42:
> fruits ˹of every type˺. And they will be honoured

**Fruits Names the Whole Menu in One Word**

One word carries the whole menu. Fawākihu — fruits — arrives without verb or preface, as if the provision of the previous verse needed no introduction beyond its own name. The grammarians call this a clarification by apposition: “a known provision” (37:41) is announced, and “fruits” explains what the announcement contains. Brevity here is not poverty but confidence; the Book trusts a single noun to open appetites that paragraphs could not. Short verses in this passage all work the same way, dropping one image at a time — provision, fruits, Gardens, thrones — so that each blessing lands separately and lingers. The Garden is furnished the way treasuries are inventoried: item by item, without hurry. What matters first is the category itself. Before kinds, quantities, and settings, the verse establishes that the provision is food, and food of the most delightful order. Everything after this word is detail; everything before it was promise. The colon of verse 41 pointed forward, and this word is what it pointed to.

**Fākihah Means Eaten for Delight, Not Need**

The noun is wider than its translation. Fākihah denotes anything eaten for enjoyment rather than necessity — the dessert, not the staple; the delight, not the diet. Al-Rāzī pressed the word for exactly this implication and found a doctrine inside it: the cuisine of Paradise serves taste rather than hunger, because in the Garden there is nothing the body lacks and no strength that food must restore. Eating continues after need has ended, which means eating was never only about need. What remains when hunger is subtracted is wish, and the fulfillment of wish brings its own satiation — pleasure as the purpose, not the byproduct. This inverts every earthly kitchen, where nutrition leads and flavor follows. Here flavor leads and nothing follows, because nothing is missing. The translation's “fruits” is therefore convenient but narrow: fruit is the closest earthly example of food eaten for joy, not the limit of what the word contains.

**Of Every Type Glosses Abundance**

The bracketed gloss — of every type — belongs to the translator, not the Arabic, which says only “fruits.” The addition is interpretive but defensible: the broken plural suggests multitude, and the commentators have always read it as comprehending kinds. Ibn Kathīr glosses the word as fruits of different kinds, served in a life of luxury where the honored are waited upon rather than waiting. Variety here is not decoration but completeness; “every type” means no desire goes unmet because no kind is missing. Earthly orchards specialize by climate and season, and every table lacks something. The Garden's table lacks nothing, because its kinds are not limited by soil or sun. Whether the gloss should stand in the text is a translator's judgment; that the meaning stands in the word is the commentators' consensus. Abundance is stated once and assumed thereafter. Every later item on the menu inherits this verse's promise of totality.

**Fruits Without Seasons or Stinginess**

Earthly fruit comes with conditions the Garden abolishes. Here a fruit has a season, a price, a distance, and an owner; it ripens, rots, and runs out, and the best clusters hang highest. There the clusters hang within reach — the image of fruit brought low for its eaters, as another passage describes clusters near at hand (69:23). Nearness removes toil, perpetuity removes anxiety, and together they remove the small economics of scarcity that govern every earthly meal. No one guards these orchards, because no one needs to; no one rations them, because they never thin. The contrast is deliberate across the whole passage: everything the Fire inflicts by force — hunger, thirst, crowding — the Garden relieves by arrangement. Fruit in this setting is not a crop but a climate, permanent as weather and free as air. To eat without season is to live without countdown.

**Taste Without Consequence Reverses the First Garden**

The first garden had one forbidden tree; this Garden has none. That contrast structures the whole doctrine of paradisal food. In Eden tasting was the test, and the wrong taste ended everything; here tasting is the reward, and no taste can end anything. Prohibition belonged to the examination hall, not the banquet hall, and examinations are over. The reversal runs deeper than permission. Eden's fruit was ordinary food made momentous by command; the Garden's fruits are momentous food made ordinary by abundance — wonder without danger, delight without disobedience. Every bite therefore un-remembers the Fall: mouths that once ate their way out of bliss now eat their way deeper in. The theology is enjoyment without trembling. Eating, the oldest human act, is finally freed from the oldest human fear. What sin poisoned at the root, mercy restores at the branch. Permission replaces probation wherever grace completes its work. The table is open because the test is over.

**The Menu Sits Inside a Place**

Food implies a place, and the verse leaves the place unnamed. Fruits grow somewhere; tables stand somewhere; eaters recline somewhere. The passage answers the implied question immediately, moving from menu to setting without a wasted word. Order matters: bounty first, then the bowers that hold it, as if to say the provision defines the place rather than the place the provision. A garden is only as good as its fruits, and these fruits have already been declared complete. Setting will add thrones and company and streams, but nothing it adds can improve what the food already guarantees. The sequence teaches appetite before architecture: hunger of the heart is answered before comfort of the eyes. Earthly hosts show the house first and serve last; heaven serves first and shows the house after. Nothing in the order is accidental, because nothing in the Garden is. Where these fruits grow comes next, as the coming verse will show.
verses.43:
> in the Gardens of Bliss

**Bliss Names the Gardens by Their Effect**

The Gardens take their name from what they do. Naʿīm — bliss, delight, ease — comes from a root that means softness and comfort: life without friction, pleasure without price. Most places are named for where they are or who built them; these are named for how they feel. The grammar makes bliss the owner and the Gardens the owned, as if delight itself held the deed. Into these Gardens the previous verse's bounty is now gathered — “fruits ˹of every type˺” (37:42) — so that food and setting authenticate each other: the place is blissful because of what grows in it, and the fruits are delightful because of where they grow. Naming by effect is also reassurance by effect. No one entering needs a map; the name is the map, promising that every step lands in softness. Etymology here is itself preaching: the word comforts before the eye sees.

**Gardens of Bliss Is a Standing Name**

The phrase is not invented for this passage; it is one of the Qur'an's standing names for Paradise, recurring wherever bounty is described — in al-Māʾidah, Yūnus, al-Ḥajj, Luqmān, al-Wāqiʿah, and al-Qalam (5:65; 10:9; 22:56; 31:8; 56:12; 68:34). It keeps company with Firdaws, ʿAdn, Khuld, and Maʾwā, the other revealed names, each stressing a different facet: height, permanence, eternity, shelter. Naʿīm stresses enjoyment. Translators have long felt the word's pull: Yusuf Ali renders the Yūnus occurrence as Gardens of Bliss, preserving the genitive's claim that bliss owns the grounds. The choice of name here is context-driven. A passage itemizing food, drink, and company reaches naturally for the name that means delight, just as passages stressing permanence reach for eternity. Names in the Book are never mere labels; each occurrence argues.

**In Locates Every Previous Blessing**

The smallest word does the largest work. Fī — in — gathers everything promised so far and houses it: the provision, the fruits, the honor all now sit inside a location. Prepositions are the passage's quiet architects; without them blessings would float unconnected, a list instead of a world. Notice what the verse does not do: it never describes walls, gates, or dimensions. Location is established by belonging rather than measurement — to be “in” bliss is to be surrounded by it on every side, held the way water holds a swimmer. Grammar becomes geography. The particle refuses to measure what it holds. Immeasurable bliss needs housing, not dimensions. The Garden is not visited but inhabited, not entered for an hour but settled forever, and the difference between those is exactly the difference this particle carries. Small words bear heavy worlds; this one bears Paradise. What the preposition joins, no exile can separate.

**Plural Gardens, Not One Garden**

The noun is plural, and plurality matters. Jannāt — Gardens — refuses to shrink Paradise to a single park with one gate and one lawn. The plural holds ranks and regions: stations proportioned to deeds, neighborhoods of the near and nearer, each community in grounds suited to it. Elsewhere the same plural gathers the same promise, as when al-Wāqiʿah seats its foremost in the same-named Gardens (56:12). Multiplicity also answers monopoly: no one crowds another, no view is blocked, no stream runs thin from sharing. Vastness is part of the bliss, not its background. A singular garden might fill; plural Gardens cannot. Plurality preaches room: there is space here for every servant ever chosen. Each garden suits its people, and each people fills its garden. Fullness without crowding is the plural's quiet miracle. No one queues for bliss.

**Bliss Against Torment: The Passage's Antithesis**

Structure turns these Gardens into an answer. The passage opened its otherworldly account with torment tasted as wages — “taste the painful torment” (37:38) — and now balances it with bliss inhabited as wages. Naʿīm stands opposite ʿadhāb alīm in every particular: pain against pleasure, tasting against dwelling, force against gift. The antithesis is moral before it is aesthetic. Two parties heard the same messengers and made opposite choices; two addresses now house the results, and the architecture refuses to blur them. One might ask why the Book lingers over both destinations at such length. The answer is pedagogical: choice needs visualized alternatives, and alternatives need weight. Weight is what these verses supply — torment with its menu of horrors, bliss with its menu of fruits — until choosing feels as serious as it is. Symmetry is theodicy made visible: equal clarity for unequal fates, freely chosen.

**The Trailing Comma Leaves the Sentence Open**

The verse ends with a comma, not a stop — and so does its predecessor. Verses 41 through 44 form a single suspended sentence: a provision announced, specified as fruits, located in Gardens, with sitters still to come. The punctuation performs the theology: blessings chained without termination, each phrase opening onto the next the way each delight opens onto another. A full stop would imply completeness, and completeness would imply limit. The passage refuses both until the scene is fully furnished. Following the commas, one experiences syntactically what the blessed experience actually — arrival without ending, gift after gift with no closing of accounts. Grammar here is not packaging but preaching: the sentence stays open because Paradise does. To read these verses aloud is to feel breath itself supplied without limit.

**Gardens Complete Their Meaning With Sitters**

Gardens complete their meaning only with sitters. A park without people is scenery; with people it becomes society, and Paradise is social to its core. The verses have so far supplied food and setting; they have not yet seated the eaters, arranged their company, or shown their faces. That absence is felt deliberately: bounty described without beneficiaries raises the question of who enjoys it, and the passage is about to answer. Thrones imply sitters, and sitters imply neighbors; bliss multiplies by company or it is not bliss. The Garden's furniture therefore points beyond itself to fellowship, and fellowship is the one luxury that cannot be stockpiled. Loneliness is the one exile Paradise never permits. Society completes scenery; bliss is social or it is not bliss. Who sits in these Gardens comes next, as the coming verse will show.
verses.44:
> facing each other on thrones

**Facing Each Other Abolishes the Back**

The participle describes furniture arrangement as moral theology. Mutaqābilīn — facing one another — means no one in this company ever sees another's back. Backs in human seating are small humiliations: the turned shoulder, the excluded auditor, the lesser guest placed behind. Ibn Kathīr, Qatādah, and Ṭabarī all draw the same inference, which the verse's economy confirms: that no one sits behind anyone is itself the honor, distributed without remainder. Faces turned toward each other declare mutual regard made permanent. The setting was named just before — “in the Gardens of Bliss” (37:43) — and the setting now fills with a geometry of respect. Arrangement preaches: where you sit is who you are, and here everyone sits facing honor. Courtesy is architecture here, built into thrones rather than requested of guests.

**Thrones Declare Rank Without Rivalry**

Surur — thrones, couches, raised seats — gives every servant what earth gives to one. A throne in the present world is a singularity: one sitter, many standers, and rivalry for the cushion. Here the plural reigns, and reigning is shared without being lessened. The Book elsewhere embroiders these seats and arrays them in rows (56:15; 52:20), and seats spouses together in shade upon them (36:56) — details this verse compresses into a single plural, trusting the wider description to furnish the scene. Rank without rivalry is the paradox only omnipotence can stage: everyone elevated, no one diminished, each throne a declaration that its occupant matters absolutely. Earthly honors shrink by sharing; these grow. Sharing here enlarges every share. The mathematics of mercy defies earthly arithmetic. To throne all guests is to abolish guests: all are hosts of honor.

**No Backs: The Commentators' Geometry**

How faces always meet without backs ever turning has exercised the commentators' imagination. Some picture a circuit so vast that seating never requires back-to-back rows, with sight, hearing, and speech so strengthened that conversation crosses any distance with ease. Others picture the thrones themselves revolving, each seat gliding toward whomsoever its occupant wishes to address. Both readings agree on what matters and differ only on mechanism: omnipotence can arrange either, and the verse binds itself to neither. The first reading's ground is divine power over space; the second's is divine power over furniture. Weighing them misses the point the verse actually presses, which is fellowship without friction. Mechanism is scenery; communion is substance. The geometry serves the sociology, not the reverse. Commentators dispute the how because the what is undisputed: perfect company.

**Envy Evicted Before the Seating**

Faces can meet because hearts have been cleaned. The Book states the prerequisite elsewhere: rancor is lifted from breasts before the seating, so that brothers sit with nothing unspoken between them (15:47). Envy is the back-turn of the soul — the inward refusal to face another's good — and it is evicted before anyone takes a throne. Al-Wāqiʿah repeats this verse's exact arrangement for its own foremost (56:16), confirming that facing is the fixed posture of honored company across sūrahs. Purification precedes placement everywhere in the Garden's logic: mouths before fruits, hearts before faces. Without that order the scene would be torture, for company without love is the definition of a crowd. With it, every face is welcome because every breast is clean. Heaven seats only reconciled people; reconciliation is part of the furniture. Cleansed breasts make facing a comfort rather than a confrontation. Purity of heart precedes posture of honor.

**Conversation Is the Feast's Main Course**

Facing exists for speech, and speech is the feast's true main course. Fruits feed the body; conversation feeds the company, and the verse arranges bodies so that talk never strains. The same sūrah will later show these very sittings in use, when the blessed turn toward each other with the ease of old friends — “turn to one another inquisitively” (37:50). Set that beside the damned, who also turn toward each other, but only for accusation — “throwing blame” (37:27). Same verb of turning, opposite eternities: interrogation here savors gall, inquisitiveness there savors joy. The arrangement of thrones thus anticipates the arrangement of talk. Furniture that faces each other produces speech that faces the same way: honest, unguarded, and kind. Eternal small talk would weary; eternal candor delights.

**Thrones Face Inward, Not Toward Spectacle**

The reciprocal pronoun deserves its own pause. Mutaqābilīn means facing each other — mutually, symmetrically, with no one left out of the exchange. What the verse pointedly does not picture is an audience: rows of seats all aimed one way at a stage, a spectacle, a distant throne. Earthly grandeur works by spectacle — one elevated figure watched by many flattened watchers. The Garden works by communion — many elevated figures beholding each other, each face a delight to the rest. There is no stage here because the company is the spectacle; no one performs and no one merely watches. Reciprocity is the highest social form the language can name, and the verse spends its whole force naming it. Thrones could have faced a single direction; that they face each other is the verse's entire argument about what heaven values.

**The Table Set, the Cups Approach**

The scene is now fully set: provision promised, fruits named, Gardens opened, thrones occupied by facing company. Each verse has added one furnishing, and none has been wasted. Food without setting would be rations; setting without company would be scenery; company without service would be an unfinished welcome. The passage knows what a feast requires and supplies it in order, moving from the general to the particular, from the estate to the table. What remains is the action itself — the pouring, the passing, the serving that turns inventory into hospitality. Diners are seated; the servers are about to move. Still life becomes living scene; description becomes event. Paradise does not display its wealth; it distributes it. Distribution is the dessert of description. Every inventory in this passage ends in generosity. The company seated, the service begins, as the coming verse will show.
verses.45:
> A drink ˹of pure wine˺ will be passed around to them from a flowing stream

**A Cup Means the Drink Inside It**

The vessel names its contents. Kaʾs in classical usage is not an empty cup but a cup with drink in it — the vessel and its fill named as one, as Jalālayn notes on exactly this verse. English “drink” catches that union better than “cup” alone, since what circulates is refreshment, not crockery. The Arabic leaves the liquid unnamed, and the translator's gloss of pure wine supplies what context and parallel passages confirm. Reserve in the noun is itself eloquent: the Book need not advertise the vintage where purity is total. The company to be served sits already arranged — “facing each other on thrones” (37:44) — so service finds its diners ready. Recall too that all of this is provision made specific: the “known provision” (37:41) now pours. Grammar moves from promise to pouring without changing subject: the same mercy, now liquid. Metonymy is hospitality: the cup stands for the care.

**Passed Around Implies Servants**

A passive verb hides active servants. Yuṭāfu — it is brought round, circulated — never names the bearers, but rounds do not walk themselves, and Ṭabarī's inference stands: attendants move among the thrones. Elsewhere the service wears gold, silver, and crystal, with vessels passed and platters borne (43:71; 76:15) — plate worthy of the guests it honors. The unnamed servers matter theologically. To be served without serving is the definition of the guest, and the Garden keeps its people guests forever: no chore interrupts the feast, no duty recalls them to labor. Circulation also implies number; one cup could be handed once, but rounds suggest many vessels, many bearers, abundance in motion. The verse shows hospitality as an institution, not an incident. Anonymity dignifies the servers and elevates the served: all attention stays on joy.

**From a Flowing Stream Promises Purity and Perpetuity**

Maʿīn describes water that flows visibly — a running spring, not a stored cask. The adjective guarantees two things at once: purity, because running water cleanses itself, and perpetuity, because a spring does not run dry. Maududi's image catches the wonder: this is no vintage pressed from rotting fruit and corn, but drink that issues from fountains as naturally as canals run. The same word waters al-Wāqiʿah's cups (56:18), binding the two passages into one doctrine of paradisal drink. Earthly wine begins in decay — fermentation is controlled rot — and ends in depletion. Heavenly wine begins in a spring and never ends at all. Source determines quality throughout the Book's logic: pure fountains, pure cups, pure delights. What flows forever cannot be finished; what cannot finish cannot disappoint.

**Pure Wine Without the World's Evils**

Purity here is not the absence of flavor but the absence of harm. The translator's “pure” renders a whole theology of paradisal wine: every delight retained, every evil removed. Muḥammad's image of the Garden's rivers includes wine expressly among water, milk, and honey, and calls it “delicious for the drinkers” (47:15) — delight asserted before any qualification. Another passage adds the moral seal: the Garden's cups carry neither idle chatter nor sin in their train (52:23), the twin poisons that earthly drinking always smuggles in. What the present verse claims by source — a flowing spring — these passages claim by effect: pleasure that never curdles into shame. The details of that immunity belong to the verses ahead, which itemize them; here the claim stands general and absolute. Wine without wound is the promise; how it holds will be shown.

**Circulation Never Ends**

The verb's tense is hospitality's calendar. An imperfect passive — it is being passed around, again and again — places circulation in continuous time, rounds without a last round. Earthly feasts wind down: pitchers empty, servants tire, guests glance at doors. This feast has no down to wind: vessels that never empty, bearers that never tire, guests that never leave. Perpetual service answers a quiet fear that abundance alone cannot silence — the fear that even plenty might end. The Garden's answer is grammatical before it is material: the action does not complete, so the joy does not either. Eternity here is not duration endured but hospitality extended, a host's hand forever mid-pour. No last call sounds where the spring never stills. Continuity comforts more than quantity ever could. Unending rounds mean unending welcome.

**Wine Unnamed Keeps the Verse Modest**

The Arabic never says the word wine. Kaʾs stands unqualified — a cup, a drink — and the identification comes only from parallel passages, where the same flowing source fills cups that the Book elsewhere names among rivers of water, milk, honey, and wine (47:15), and where the same word maʿīn describes paradisal cups whose effects the passage then qualifies (56:18–19). Why the reserve? Partly euphemism: the Book often approaches delicate subjects obliquely before speaking plainly, letting context carry what bluntness would cheapen. Partly focus: what matters in this verse is service and source, not vintage — the passing around and the flowing stream. The translator's gloss of pure wine therefore reports a sound inference rather than an explicit term. Restraint is rhetoric here: purity so total it need not name itself.

**The Stream's Gifts Get Described**

The verse ends, like verse 41, with a colon: announcement now, description next. What has been established is the service — its vessel, its bearers, its source. What remains is the portrait — how the drink looks, how it tastes, what it does and does not do. The passage rations its pleasures the way the Garden rations nothing: one delight per verse, each given room to shine. The sequence teaches patience along with anticipation; the cup is raised slowly, that desire may ripen before drinking. Withholding the description heightens it — the coming portrait lands harder for the waiting. Colons are promises; this one promises a portrait. The cup circles closer with every verse. Anticipation is the first sip, and it is served here. What flows in the cup comes next, as the coming verse will show.
verses.46:
> crystal-white, delicious to drink

**White Is the First Thing Seen**

Color precedes flavor in the verse's order. Bayḍāʾ — white, bright white — meets the eye before ladhdhah meets the tongue.
